From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Severe latency and errors affecting inference on /v1/generate — urgent

Quick triage summary:

What we see
- Hosted-api (us-west) saw a sustained increase in request queue depth (median queue size up 4–7x) starting 08:40.
- p95 increased from ~180ms to ~1.2s; p99 from ~420ms to ~3.4s.
- Error rate (5xx) rose from 0.2% to ~4% during the spike.

Probable cause
- A recent change in the batching scheduler (deferred batching window extension rolled out to a portion of hosts last week) widened batching windows under bursty inputs. Under a short burst pattern, this caused more requests to accumulate and form large batches, amplifying tail latency on the GPU kernels and growing KV-cache pressure.

What I pulled
- pipeline-dump-20261203.log (attached): shows long per-batch execution times and multiple retransmissions on the request path.
- Hot hosts: hw-node-44/47/51 in us-west.

Immediate mitigation steps in progress
1) Roll back deferred batching window change on the affected host pool (in progress).
2) Temporarily set max_batch_size=64 for the model family servicing Acme traffic to limit per-batch execution time.
3) Opened INF-3219 (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3219) and pinned a priority tag.

I’m attaching the pipeline dump and a quick snippet of the timing histogram. Will update with confirmation once rollback completes.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior SRE, Serving Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, jonas@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 11:30:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Severe latency and errors affecting inference on /v1/generate — urgent

Following Soojin’s findings, I ran a short simulation against a staging snapshot of the us-west pool:
- Reducing the deferred batching window and capping max_batch_size to 64 brings p95 down to ~220ms in the sim (from simulated large batches).
- Disabling deferred batching entirely reduces KV pressure and eliminates the retransmission cycle in the sim.

Planned immediate ops actions (target 2–4 hours):
- Rollback deferred-window for affected hosts (Soojin is rolling now).
- Apply max_batch_size=64 and increase fast-path preemption frequency for inference threads.
- Route Acme traffic to a warm dedicated fallback pool for the next 4 hours; costs will be logged against incident.

Requesting Marissa and Sean to approve temporary routing and to evaluate whether SLA credit/comp is needed depending on final outage duration.

Ethan
Ethan Park
Lead, Inference Performance
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Diane Price <diane.price@acmecorp.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com, ethan_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 13:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Severe latency and errors affecting inference on /v1/generate — urgent

Diane — update and next steps:

What happened: our serving runtime rolled out a deferred-batching window extension to a subset of us-west hosts last week. Under a bursty traffic pattern you’re seeing, that widened window allowed large multisecond batches to form which increased tail latency and generated spikes in error retries.

What we’re doing (in-flight):
- Rollback of the batching change completed at ~12:05 PST for the affected host pool.
- We capped batch size and routed Acme traffic to a warm dedicated pool while we validate stability.
- Engineers are running a post-fix verification; preliminary telemetry shows p95 returning toward baseline.

ETA and ask:
- Complete verification and full traffic normalization by 15:30 PST today.
- We’d like permission to route 30% of traffic to the dedicated fallback for 4 hours to ensure no residual tail effects — this may incur a short-term cost that we will cover in the incident report.

We will also open a compensation ticket pending final outage duration; please flag if you want immediate SLA credit now.

Thanks for your patience — we’ll follow up with a final post-incident summary.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
